newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's mortgage bank issues $39.4 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's mortgage bank issues $39.4 mln bonds.

text.p: Morocco's Credit Immobilier et Hotelier issued 375 million dirhams ($39.4 million) in 15-year debenture bonds at a rate of 10.5 percent.
The bank, which is listed on the Casablanca bourse, announced the bond issue in Le Matin newspaper on Tuesday and said subscriptions would be open until June 27.
It said the issue consisted of 2,500 bonds each worth 150,000 dirhams. The bonds will be introduced on the stock exchange on July 1, 1997.
For the first time, the issue is not backed by the state, a stockbroker said.

"Liberalisation of the finance market, competition and the generalisation of CIH activities means that it no longer benefits from the state guarantee except for social housing," the newspaper advertisement said.
Last year, CIH issued up to 1.05 billion dirhams in state-guaranteed debentures.
The state owns a majority stake in the bank, which holds 65 percent of the Moroccan mortgage market. The bank is on a list of companies due for privatisation this year.

Hotels have borrowings with CIH totalling 5.5 billion dirhams while overall doubtful debts amounted to 3.5 billion dirhams at the end of 1996, a spokeswoman at Upline Securities brokerage told Reuters.
last traded on Monday at 293 dirhams.
